emb:L2044690222.model_family: deep learning image classifiers (binary and multi-class CNNs) with occlusion sensitivity mapping
emb:L2044690222.clinical_problem: differential diagnosis of rare bone diseases from hand radiographs
emb:L2044690222.patient_population: children undergoing hand radiographs for bone age assessment, with 45 different rare bone diseases (RBDs) compared to unaffected controls
emb:L2044690222.model_description: Bone2Gene takes a hand radiograph as input and first classifies whether it shows a rare bone disease (RBD) versus not, then, for RBD-positive cases, a second multi-class model predicts which of ten RBD groups is most likely. It was trained and evaluated with 5-fold cross-validation on 5,623 multi-institutional hand radiographs from 2,471 patients with 45 RBDs and 1,382 controls, using occlusion sensitivity mapping and embedding analysis to visualize the features driving each prediction.
emb:L2044690222.dataset_size: 5,623 multi-institutional hand radiographs from 2,471 patients with 45 different RBDs and 1,382 unaffected controls
emb:L2044690222.headline_result: affected vs unaffected classifier: balanced accuracy 85.5%; ten-class classifier: balanced top-1 accuracy 76.6%, top-3 accuracy exceeding 90%

emb:L2044875744.exclusion_reason: voxel-based morphometry statistical analysis (SPM12), not an AI/ML model

emb:L2044449564.exclusion_reason: population age not stated; cohort name references children/parents but ages of the ultrasound-scanned subjects are not given in the abstract

emb:L2044449587.clinical_problem: classification of autism spectrum disorder and prediction of social cognitive ability from brain functional connectivity
emb:L2044449587.patient_population: 69 children (34 with autism spectrum disorder, 35 typically developing)
emb:L2044449587.model_description: The NBS-Predict machine-learning framework was applied to resting-state fMRI functional connectivity data from 69 children to build a classifier distinguishing autism spectrum disorder (ASD) from typically developing children, and a regression model predicting each child's Social Responsiveness Scale (SRS-2) social cognition score from the same connectivity patterns.
emb:L2044449587.headline_result: FC-based classifier distinguished ASD from typically developing children with 62.8% accuracy; regression model predicted individual SRS-2 scores (r = 0.252, p < 0.001)

emb:L2045066212.exclusion_reason: adult population undergoing medication abortion; model uses clinical and ultrasound-derived variables, not image-based radiology AI

emb:L2044689715.model_family: twin-aware multimodal deep learning framework: 3D CNN for neuroimaging with prototype-based residual encoders for behavioral/phenotypic data, combined by optimized weighted late fusion
emb:L2044689715.clinical_problem: early prediction of adolescent anxiety disorder
emb:L2044689715.patient_population: adolescents from the QTAB (Queensland Twin Adolescent Brain) dataset, a twin cohort
emb:L2044689715.model_description: A multimodal deep learning framework applies a 3D convolutional neural network to adolescent brain MRI and prototype-based residual encoders to behavioral and phenotypic questionnaire data, then combines the modality-specific outputs through optimized weighted late fusion (23% MRI, 63% questionnaire, 14% phenotypic) to predict risk of adolescent anxiety disorder in a twin cohort.
emb:L2044689715.headline_result: AUC 0.8935 (95% CI 0.792-0.969), an 11-percentage-point gain over the best unimodal (questionnaire-only) baseline (AUC 0.7766), with 85.7% sensitivity and 87.3% specificity
emb:L2044689715.study_design: retrospective technical development / predictive modeling study

emb:L2044176335.model_family: heterogeneous ensemble of a MedSAM-based vision transformer with low-rank adaptation and a self-configuring nnU-Net v2, fused via probability averaging
emb:L2044176335.clinical_problem: automated angle of progression (AOP) measurement for intrapartum fetal head descent assessment
emb:L2044176335.patient_population: pregnant patients undergoing transperineal ultrasound during labor for fetal head descent assessment
emb:L2044176335.model_description: A dual-model ensemble combines a MedSAM-based vision transformer with low-rank adaptation and a self-configuring nnU-Net v2 to segment relevant structures on transperineal ultrasound images. The segmentation is used to compute the angle of progression (AOP), a measure of fetal head descent during labor, via closed-form tangent-line geometry on fitted ellipses. The model was trained on 4,000 images and evaluated on an independent set of 1,101 images.
emb:L2044176335.dataset_size: 4,000 training images; independent validation set of 1,101 images (858 limited descent, 243 advanced descent)
emb:L2044176335.headline_result: F1 0.865 (95% CI 0.831-0.896), AUC 0.960 (0.947-0.971), sensitivity 86.8%, specificity 96.0%; mean absolute AOP error 5.93 degrees (median 4.10)
emb:L2044176335.study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study

emb:L2044689598.exclusion_reason: near-infrared spectroscopy wearable device with machine learning analysis; not a radiology imaging modality

emb:L2044872798.model_family: multimodal machine-learning markers derived from resting-state functional and structural MRI
emb:L2044872798.clinical_problem: prediction of cognitive functioning and its longitudinal trajectory in children with ADHD
emb:L2044872798.patient_population: children with and without ADHD from the longitudinal Oregon ADHD-1000 study
emb:L2044872798.model_description: Multimodal markers were developed from resting-state functional and structural brain MRI to predict cognitive functioning in a longitudinal, ADHD-enriched cohort of children (Oregon ADHD-1000, n=594, 1,053 annual timepoints). The markers predict both between-child differences in cognitive functioning and within-child changes over time, and performed comparably in children with and without ADHD.
emb:L2044872798.headline_result: out-of-sample prediction accuracy r=0.459; explained 29.09% of interindividual variance, 33.48% of intraindividual cognitive trajectories, and 60.87% of intraindividual age-related cognitive development
emb:L2044872798.study_design: prospective longitudinal cohort, predictive modeling study

emb:L2042541482.model_family: review of hybrid LSTM, CNN, transformer and explainable-AI (XAI) models
emb:L2042541482.clinical_problem: prediction of fetal weight, delivery mode, and fetal gender using antenatal ultrasound and clinical data
emb:L2042541482.patient_population: pregnant women in antenatal care, across studies published 2000-2024
emb:L2042541482.model_description: This systematic review evaluates machine learning and deep learning models that combine maternal, fetal, and ultrasound data to predict fetal weight, mode of delivery, and fetal gender. It compares hybrid LSTM, CNN, transformer, and explainable-AI approaches against traditional statistical methods across studies published between 2000 and 2024.

emb:L2038072573.model_family: deep learning MRI reconstruction algorithm (AIR Recon DL) combined with U-Net segmentation
emb:L2038072573.clinical_problem: screening for fetal growth restriction (FGR) and placental insufficiency
emb:L2038072573.patient_population: 120 pregnant women, gestational age 24-36 weeks, divided into FGR (n=60) and non-FGR (n=60) groups undergoing fetal MRI
emb:L2038072573.model_description: Fetal MRI images were reconstructed using the commercial AIR Recon deep-learning algorithm to improve image quality. A U-Net segmentation model delineated the fetal abdomen on the reconstructed MRI to calculate estimated fetal weight (combined with ultrasound-measured femur length via the Hadlock formula), which was used to diagnose fetal growth restriction and placental insufficiency against birth weight as reference.
emb:L2038072573.release_evidence: images reconstructed using the 'AIR Recon Deep Learning (DL) algorithm', a named GE scanner reconstruction product; femur length measured on a GE Voluson E10 system
emb:L2038072573.dataset_size: 120 pregnant women (60 FGR, 60 non-FGR), gestational age 24-36 weeks
emb:L2038072573.headline_result: Dice coefficient for segmentation 0.892 +/- 0.021, EFW mean absolute error 148.2 g, FGR diagnostic accuracy 91.7% (AUROC 0.938) vs manual assessment 84.5% (AUROC 0.864, p=0.032)

emb:L2040976018.model_family: ghost convolution-based YOLOv11 lightweight object detector
emb:L2040976018.clinical_problem: fracture detection on pediatric wrist radiographs
emb:L2040976018.patient_population: children undergoing wrist radiography (GRAZPEDWRI-DX public dataset)
emb:L2040976018.model_description: G-YOLOv11 is a lightweight computer-aided detection system for fractures on pediatric wrist X-rays, built on the YOLOv11 object detector with ghost convolution layers that generate the same feature maps as standard convolution with fewer computations. It was evaluated on the public GRAZPEDWRI-DX pediatric wrist radiograph dataset against the standard YOLOv11l model.
emb:L2040976018.release_evidence: Code and models are available at https://github.com/AbdesselamFerdi/G-YOLOv11
emb:L2040976018.dataset_size: GRAZPEDWRI-DX public pediatric wrist radiograph dataset
emb:L2040976018.headline_result: mAP@0.5 of 0.535, inference time 2.4 ms; 13.6% lower mAP@0.5 than standard YOLOv11l with a 68.7% reduction in model size
emb:L2040976018.study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study

emb:L2041558079.exclusion_reason: population age not stated in abstract; source datasets (chest X-ray pneumonia and NIH databases) not described as pediatric

emb:L2041591580.model_family: instance segmentation network with a lightweight Vision Transformer (EfficientViT), dilated convolutions, and E-Focal Loss
emb:L2041591580.clinical_problem: segmentation of fetal heart anatomical structures for congenital heart disease (CHD) screening and prenatal diagnosis
emb:L2041591580.patient_population: fetuses undergoing standard fetal heart ultrasound views (newly constructed FH-3K dataset)
emb:L2041591580.model_description: FHSS-Net is a deep learning instance segmentation model for fetal heart ultrasound images. It combines a lightweight Vision Transformer module (EfficientViT) for long-range feature modeling, dilated convolutions for a wider receptive field, and an E-Focal Loss to address class imbalance, segmenting ten key anatomical structures across five standard fetal heart views. It was developed and benchmarked on the newly constructed FH-3K fetal heart ultrasound dataset.
emb:L2041591580.dataset_size: FH-3K dataset: five standard fetal heart views, ten annotated anatomical structures
emb:L2041591580.headline_result: 93.7% localization accuracy and 92% segmentation accuracy across ten anatomical structures under five-fold cross-validation, outperforming mainstream models
emb:L2041591580.study_design: retrospective technical development / segmentation benchmark study

emb:L2042500034.clinical_problem: right ventricular functional assessment (fractional area change) in pediatric echocardiography
emb:L2042500034.patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing echocardiography (664 pediatric echocardiograms)
emb:L2042500034.model_description: Multiple deep learning segmentation models were trained on 664 pediatric echocardiograms to automatically delineate the right ventricle and calculate right ventricular fractional area change (RVFAC), a measure of RV function. The best-performing model (FCBFormer architecture) was compared against ground-truth and four expert readers in a blinded evaluation to assess whether it reduces inter-observer variability in RV assessment.
emb:L2042500034.headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 0.926, mean absolute error 5.913% for RVFAC prediction; model-generated segmentation favored over human segmentation in 57.3% of evaluated cases
emb:L2042500034.study_design: retrospective diagnostic accuracy study with reader comparison

emb:L2043406743.exclusion_reason: dental imaging (panoramic radiographs for caries/periapical infection), an excluded modality

emb:L2044275065.exclusion_reason: broad narrative review of AI in pediatric endocrinology (hormonal, lifestyle, wearable and imaging data); automated bone age assessment is only a minor mentioned component, not the focus

emb:L2044815890.exclusion_reason: electrocardiography-based prediction model; not a diagnostic imaging (radiology) modality

emb:L2043923408.clinical_problem: automated segmentation of the postoperative resection cavity after epilepsy surgery to quantify extent of tissue resection
emb:L2043923408.patient_population: children and adults who underwent epilepsy surgery, from the multicentre MELD project (27 centres) and the EPISURG dataset, with a range of resection locations and pathologies
emb:L2043923408.model_description: MELD-PostOp is a deep learning tool built on nnU-Net that automatically segments the surgical resection cavity on postoperative 3D T1-weighted brain MRI following epilepsy surgery. It was trained on 965 manually and semi-automatically segmented cases from 27 centres (children and adults, temporal and extra-temporal resections) and evaluated on stratified and independent held-out test cohorts against existing tools (Epic-CHOP, ResectVol).
emb:L2043923408.release_evidence: "This open-source tool facilitates large-scale quantitative analysis"
emb:L2043923408.dataset_size: 965 subjects for training across 27 centres; stratified test cohort n=50; independent test cohort n=87
emb:L2043923408.headline_result: median Dice similarity coefficient 0.85 and HD95 3.61 on the combined test cohort, outperforming Epic-CHOP (DSC 0.68) and ResectVol (DSC 0.66); detected 99% (135/137) of resection cavities
emb:L2043923408.study_design: retrospective multi-center technical development / segmentation validation study

emb:L2043847964.exclusion_reason: EEG-based functional brain age analysis; not a diagnostic imaging (radiology) modality

emb:L2043761891.clinical_problem: forensic age assessment via distal radial epiphyseal fusion timing (medico-legal age-of-majority determination)
emb:L2043761891.patient_population: Northwest European and Middle Eastern individuals aged 13-25 years, including asylum seekers, assessed at German clinical sites and reception facilities
emb:L2043761891.model_description: A fully automated ultrasound device assesses distal radial epiphyseal fusion status. Gradient-boosting machine learning models (LightGBM) were trained on 830 high-quality ultrasound datasets to classify fusion status against reference ages (documented birthdate or Greulich-Pyle bone age), evaluated with leave-one-out cross-validation across sex- and population-specific age thresholds, for forensic determination of whether an individual has reached a legally relevant age threshold.
emb:L2043761891.dataset_size: 1,061 recordings; 830 high-quality ultrasound datasets analyzed, ages 13-25 years
emb:L2043761891.headline_result: AUC approximately 0.81-1.00 near optimal thresholds; optimal discrimination thresholds ranged 17.0-18.5 years across sex/population groups

emb:L2043746724.model_family: graph theory network analysis combined with machine learning on functional brain network features
emb:L2043746724.clinical_problem: identifying social and psychological predictors of longitudinal functional brain network development in mid-adolescence
emb:L2043746724.patient_population: mid-adolescents from low-socioeconomic-status contexts, longitudinal 2-year fMRI cohort (n=65)
emb:L2043746724.model_description: Graph theory measures were computed from a 2-year longitudinal resting-state fMRI dataset of 65 mid-adolescents. Machine learning analysis was used to identify which factors, among parental education, community violence exposure, IQ, and a measured psychological disposition ('transcendent thinking'), best predicted changes in functional brain network organization (segregation, integration, entropy, energy) over the study period.
emb:L2043746724.headline_result: machine learning identified transcendent thinking and community violence exposure, but not IQ, as the principal predictors of functional brain network change across groups

emb:L2043922950.model_family: AI algorithm for gestational age estimation from handheld blind-sweep ultrasound (commercial product)
emb:L2043922950.clinical_problem: gestational age estimation for antenatal care and pre-eclampsia risk screening in low-resource settings
emb:L2043922950.patient_population: 969 pregnant women at 13 health facilities across Kenya, Ghana and South Africa, presenting 11+0 to 13+6 weeks' gestation with follow-up to 27+6 weeks
emb:L2043922950.model_description: This study protocol describes a prospective multi-country accuracy study of the commercial Intelligent Ultrasound ScanNav FetalCheck AI system, which estimates gestational age from handheld blind-sweep ultrasound scans performed by a trained midwife using a GE VScan Air device. Its accuracy will be compared against conventional fetal biometry (crown-rump length) performed by a trained sonographer as the reference standard, in 969 women across 13 facilities in Ghana, Kenya, and South Africa.
emb:L2043922950.release_evidence: "the AI-based Intelligent Ultrasound ScanNav FetalCheck system (experimental)"
emb:L2043922950.dataset_size: 969 pregnant women, 13 health facilities in 3 countries

emb:L2043922853.model_family: 3D point cloud geometric processing pipeline (segmentation plus classification)
emb:L2043922853.clinical_problem: radiation-free triage screening for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS)
emb:L2043922853.patient_population: adolescents screened for scoliosis, multi-center validation cohort
emb:L2043922853.model_description: PointScol is a radiation-free triage system that processes 3D point clouds of the back surface, obtained by optical/depth scanning rather than X-ray, to screen for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis. It first segments the dorsal region of interest, then classifies spinal deformity, acting as a binary screening gate at a 10-degree Cobb angle threshold and as a 5-class severity grading tool to guide referral urgency. It was validated on a multi-center dataset.
emb:L2043922853.headline_result: 100.00% sensitivity in the external cohort for the primary screening task (10-degree Cobb angle threshold)
emb:L2043922853.study_design: technical development / multi-center diagnostic accuracy study

emb:L2043673929.exclusion_reason: MRI radiomics imaging of the placenta and uterus (maternal anatomy) for placenta accreta spectrum; not fetal or pediatric imaging

emb:L2043673963.model_family: pre-trained deep learning super-resolution model (GAMBAS) for ultra-low-field MRI
emb:L2043673963.clinical_problem: brain volume assessment and neurodevelopmental correlation using portable ultra-low-field MRI in small-for-gestational-age vs appropriate-for-gestational-age children
emb:L2043673963.patient_population: 64 children aged 3-5 years (from a birth cohort of 180 children: 90 small-for-gestational-age, 90 appropriate-for-gestational-age), scanned with a portable 64mT ultra-low-field MRI system
emb:L2043673963.model_description: The pre-trained GAMBAS deep learning model generated super-resolved images from ultra-low-field (64mT, Hyperfine Swoop) brain MRI scans of children. Brain volumes derived from the super-resolved images were compared against high-field MRI in a subset for validation, and correlated with neurodevelopmental scores (Malawi Developmental Assessment Tool) to compare small-for-gestational-age and appropriate-for-gestational-age children.
emb:L2043673963.dataset_size: 64 children aged 3-5 years from a cohort of 180 (90 SGA, 90 AGA); ground-truth comparison subset n=10
emb:L2043673963.headline_result: strong correlation and high concordance between super-resolved and high-field brain volumes for total intracranial volume, white matter, cerebral cortex, basal ganglia and thalamus; correlation between super-resolved volumes and neurodevelopmental (MDAT) z-scores was not statistically significant

emb:L2043922496.clinical_problem: image quality improvement for neonatal brain MRI to support assessment of early myelinating structures
emb:L2043922496.patient_population: 15 neonates undergoing 3D T1-weighted brain MRI at 3 Tesla
emb:L2043922496.model_description: A deep learning image reconstruction algorithm was applied at low, medium and high denoising levels to 3D T1-weighted brain MRI scans of 15 neonates. Three radiologists rated image quality (signal-to-noise, artifacts, clarity) of eight early myelinating brain structures on a 4-point scale, and objective signal-to-noise and contrast-to-noise ratios were measured across denoising levels.
emb:L2043922496.headline_result: overall increase in all image-quality categories and conspicuity of early myelinating structures with increasing denoising; significant increases in apparent SNR and CNR for nearly all pairwise comparisons
emb:L2043922496.study_design: prospective single-center image quality evaluation, multireader study

emb:L2037814363.model_family: TensorFlow-based GLCM texture feature extraction with a support vector machine (SVM) classifier
emb:L2037814363.clinical_problem: prediction of neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (NRDS) risk in gestational diabetes mellitus pregnancies from fetal lung texture
emb:L2037814363.patient_population: 50 pregnant patients with gestational diabetes mellitus; standardized four-chamber-view fetal ultrasound images
emb:L2037814363.model_description: A TensorFlow-based framework extracted 342 gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) texture features from fetal lung regions on standardized four-chamber-view ultrasound images in 50 pregnancies complicated by gestational diabetes. A support vector machine classifier used these texture features, combined with uterine artery Doppler pulsatility index, to stratify risk of neonatal respiratory distress syndrome.
emb:L2037814363.dataset_size: 50 patients with gestational diabetes mellitus (22 with NRDS, 28 controls)
emb:L2037814363.headline_result: standalone AI pulmonary texture analysis: 86.4% sensitivity, 78.6% specificity for NRDS prediction (kappa=0.67); combined AI plus uterine artery PI model: 92.0% overall accuracy (46/50)

emb:L2039934968.model_family: self-supervised representation learning combined with an optimized heterogeneous ensemble of lightweight base learners
emb:L2039934968.clinical_problem: early diagnosis of biliary atresia from sonographic gallbladder images
emb:L2039934968.patient_population: infants/children evaluated for biliary atresia by sonographic gallbladder imaging
emb:L2039934968.model_description: SSL-OHE combines self-supervised representation learning (online clustering-based pretraining initialized from a large general vision dataset) with a heterogeneous ensemble of lightweight base learners, fine-tuned to classify biliary atresia from sonographic gallbladder images. A numerical optimization step determines ensemble weights across base learners to improve diagnostic performance despite the rarity and imbalance of biliary atresia data.
emb:L2039934968.study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study

emb:L2039981433.model_family: hybrid-branch convolutional neural network (MobileNetV2 backbone with an attention module)
emb:L2039981433.clinical_problem: classification of standard fetal brain ultrasound planes for prenatal screening
emb:L2039981433.patient_population: public fetal ultrasound dataset used for prenatal screening
emb:L2039981433.model_description: AC_Branch_MobileNet is a lightweight convolutional neural network that automatically classifies fetal ultrasound images into three standard fetal brain planes (trans-ventricular, trans-cerebellar, trans-thalamic) to support prenatal screening. It uses a MobileNetV2 backbone with an added attention-based branch structure, preceded by an unsharp-masking preprocessing step to reduce speckle noise, and was evaluated on a public fetal ultrasound dataset.
emb:L2039981433.dataset_size: public fetal ultrasound dataset (exact count not stated)
emb:L2039981433.headline_result: accuracy 95.11%, precision 94.62%, recall 94.39%, F1-score 94.50%, outperforming the best baseline by up to 7.43% in accuracy
emb:L2039981433.study_design: retrospective technical development / classification benchmark study

emb:L2040009264.model_family: segmentation pipeline combining an ROI detection network, a foundation model for instance generation, and an instance classifier network, trained with semi-automated annotation and curriculum learning
emb:L2040009264.clinical_problem: bone segmentation on pediatric hand radiographs to support bone analysis across a wide age range
emb:L2040009264.patient_population: 552 hand X-ray images of children from the public RSNA and Digital Hand Atlas (DHA) datasets, diverse ages and racial backgrounds
emb:L2040009264.model_description: PedVision is a segmentation pipeline for pediatric hand X-rays designed to scale across ages without manual annotation. It uses a region-of-interest network to localize relevant areas, a foundation model to generate instance-level predictions, and an instance classifier network to map instances to 19 hand bones grouped into 5 classes, trained via a semi-automated annotation framework and curriculum learning across rounds of increasing model complexity. It was evaluated on 552 hand X-rays from the public RSNA and Digital Hand Atlas datasets against U-Net, DeepLabV3+, and SegFormer baselines.
emb:L2040009264.release_evidence: "The project is open source at github.com/mohofar/PedVision"
emb:L2040009264.dataset_size: 552 hand X-ray images of children (RSNA and Digital Hand Atlas datasets)
emb:L2040009264.headline_result: for pediatric cases (0-7 years): 11.08% Dice improvement over U-Net on RSNA and 7.68% on DHA; 14.43%/14.78% improvement over DeepLabV3+; 8.16%/1.91% improvement over the best SegFormer variant
emb:L2040009264.study_design: retrospective technical development / segmentation benchmark study

emb:L2040647391.exclusion_reason: segmentation of maternal levator ani muscle/pelvic floor for postpartum pelvic organ prolapse; not a pediatric population

emb:L2040772263.model_family: review of deep learning segmentation and registration architectures (CNNs, attention mechanisms) for infant brain MRI
emb:L2040772263.clinical_problem: segmentation and registration of infant brain MRI to support studying neonatal brain development and diagnosing early brain disease
emb:L2040772263.model_description: This review surveys more than 100 papers on deep learning-based segmentation and registration of infant brain MRI, covering neural network architectures, attention mechanisms, and data processing techniques, and discusses the performance metrics used to evaluate these methods relative to techniques developed for adult brain MRI.

emb:L2040796100.model_family: convolutional neural network with heat-map regression key-point detection and spatial/channel attention
emb:L2040796100.body_region: hand and wrist (radius, ulna, carpal bones)
emb:L2040796100.clinical_problem: Tanner-Whitehouse 3 (TW3) bone age assessment including carpal-bone scoring, for diagnosis of skeletal growth abnormalities
emb:L2040796100.patient_population: children and infants undergoing hand radiography for skeletal maturity assessment
emb:L2040796100.model_description: A two-stage deep learning pipeline first uses a heat-map regression key-point detection network with spatial configuration to locate and segment all 20 TW3 regions of interest on a hand radiograph, then a skeletal-maturity classification network with spatial and channel attention predicts maturity scores and bone age for both the radius-ulna-short-bone (TW3-RUS) and carpal bone (TW3-C) series, extending prior automated methods that could only assess TW3-RUS.
emb:L2040796100.dataset_size: 5,235 left hand radiographs of children of different ages
emb:L2040796100.headline_result: mean absolute error of bone age 0.42 years (TW3-RUS) and 0.44 years (TW3-C)
emb:L2040796100.study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study

emb:L2040862311.model_family: 3D multi-view dual encoder-decoder CNN with attention mechanism
emb:L2040862311.clinical_problem: segmentation of focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) lesions for pre-surgical epilepsy evaluation
emb:L2040862311.patient_population: patients with intractable epilepsy due to focal cortical dysplasia, adults and children
emb:L2040862311.model_description: A 3D deep learning model with a multi-view dual encoder-decoder architecture and residual connections segments focal cortical dysplasia lesions on brain MRI. It processes FLAIR MRI volumes together with corresponding cortical thickness maps through two encoders linked by a 3D attention mechanism, and two decoders for dual-task learning using ground-truth-derived distance maps, intended to assist neuroradiologists in presurgical evaluation of epilepsy patients including both children and adults.
emb:L2040862311.headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 4.8% and 2.3% higher than state-of-the-art 2D and 3D FCD segmentation methods, respectively
emb:L2040862311.study_design: retrospective technical development / segmentation benchmark study

emb:L2040898407.model_family: self-distillation hybrid-attention network (ResNet50 backbone with Squeeze-and-Excitation and Spatial Transformer attention modules)
emb:L2040898407.clinical_problem: automatic age estimation from head MRI in children, as a radiation-free alternative to radiographic age estimation
emb:L2040898407.model_description: SDHA is a self-distillation network with Squeeze-and-Excitation and Spatial Transformer attention modules built on a ResNet50 backbone (teacher) with early-exit student branches, trained on 3T head MRI to estimate a child's age without ionizing radiation. Grad-CAM visualization showed the model attends to age-relevant dental, facial, and brain structures. It was compared against manual assessment and conventional CNN methods.
emb:L2040898407.headline_result: SDHA mean absolute error 0.34 years vs manual method 0.44 years; 63.4% MAE reduction vs a non-distilled SENet (MAE 0.93 years); prediction time reduced from 120 s (manual) to 0.11 s per subject
emb:L2040898407.study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study

emb:L2040912038.model_family: deep learning pipeline: GAN-based data augmentation, hybrid U-Net segmentation (UDANet) with dilated convolution and decoder attention, IpLU activation
emb:L2040912038.clinical_problem: automated Cobb angle measurement for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) severity grading
emb:L2040912038.patient_population: adolescents/children with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis undergoing spine X-ray, including presurgical severe cases
emb:L2040912038.model_description: SCANet is an end-to-end pipeline for Cobb angle measurement from spine X-rays in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis. It augments training images with geometric transformations and a generative adversarial network, segments the vertebral region with a hybrid U-Net (UDANet) that incorporates dilated convolutions and a decoder attention module, derives a vertebral compression ratio from the segmentation, and computes the Cobb angle from these segmentation coordinates.
emb:L2040912038.headline_result: 98.65% accuracy in Cobb angle measurement, 2.06% and 4.16% higher than DNN and CNN comparators respectively
emb:L2040912038.study_design: retrospective technical development / measurement accuracy study

emb:L2041102286.exclusion_reason: optical 3D body-shape scanning of pregnant women; not a radiology imaging modality

emb:L2043178419.exclusion_reason: broad narrative review of AI in neonatal respiratory care spanning physiological monitoring, electronic health records, and imaging; not primarily focused on radiology imaging AI

emb:L2043284063.model_family: self-supervised transfer learning binary classification models
emb:L2043284063.clinical_problem: noninvasive molecular subtyping of pediatric low-grade glioma (BRAF Fusion vs BRAF Mutation vs Wild Type) from MRI
emb:L2043284063.patient_population: pediatric patients with low-grade glioma (pLGG); external validation cohorts from the Hospital for Sick Children (n=336, 2000-2018; and n=87, 2019-2023)
emb:L2043284063.model_description: Three binary self-supervised transfer-learning classification models, pretrained on data from Dana-Farber Cancer Institute/Boston Children's Hospital, were externally evaluated on T2-weighted MRI from two independent cohorts at the Hospital for Sick Children to classify the molecular subtype of pediatric low-grade glioma (BRAF Fusion, BRAF Mutation, or Wild Type). Manually annotated tumor segmentations were used as input, and per-class probabilities from the three models were combined via a softmax function to compute a multi-class AUC.
emb:L2043284063.headline_result: macro-average AUC 0.7671 on the newer dataset, 0.6463 on the older dataset
emb:L2043284063.study_design: retrospective external validation diagnostic accuracy study

emb:L2037818707.model_family: review of deep learning-based medical imaging analysis systems
emb:L2037818707.clinical_problem: AI-assisted screening and diagnosis in pediatric orthopedics: developmental dysplasia of the hip, scoliosis, and pediatric fractures
emb:L2037818707.model_description: This Chinese-language review surveys applications and challenges of artificial intelligence in pediatric orthopedics, focusing on deep learning-based medical imaging analysis systems used for early screening and diagnosis of developmental dysplasia of the hip, scoliosis, and pediatric fractures, as well as AI's role in personalized treatment planning by integrating imaging with biomechanical models and in surgical navigation. It discusses barriers including data quality, clinical workflow integration, and privacy/ethical governance.

emb:L2043217536.model_family: AI decision-support model (architecture not specified) for pneumoperitoneum detection
emb:L2043217536.clinical_problem: detection of pneumoperitoneum (free air) on neonatal radiographs, a time-critical surgical emergency
emb:L2043217536.patient_population: 14 readers (pediatric radiologists, neonatologists, radiology residents) interpreting 125 neonatal radiographs
emb:L2043217536.model_description: This multi-reader multi-center study evaluated how AI assistance for detecting pneumoperitoneum on neonatal radiographs affects clinician verification behavior. Fourteen readers of varying specialty and seniority (pediatric radiologists, neonatologists, radiology residents) interpreted 125 neonatal radiographs across two sessions, under three conditions: unaided, aided by a reliable AI, and aided by an error-injected (unreliable) AI, with outcomes including diagnostic accuracy, deliberation time, and automation bias.
emb:L2043217536.headline_result: neonatologists overrode 91.6% of AI errors under error-injected AI (OR 4.16 vs unaided baseline, p=0.020); radiology residents accepted incorrect advice from reliable AI in 52.0% of discordant cases vs 20.0% for pediatric radiologists (p=0.016)

emb:L2042963883.exclusion_reason: dental imaging (panoramic radiographs, teeth detection/segmentation), an excluded modality

emb:L2042640286.exclusion_reason: unified clinical decision-support framework using structured clinical and ultrasound-derived variables with logistic regression, not an image-based radiology AI model

emb:L2036028779.model_family: MLOps framework encompassing the model development/deployment pipeline for fetal ultrasound plane classification
emb:L2036028779.clinical_problem: operationalizing machine learning models for fetal ultrasound standard-plane detection to support prenatal screening workflow
emb:L2036028779.patient_population: fetal ultrasound imaging for prenatal care
emb:L2036028779.model_description: FetalMLOps is a ten-step MLOps framework adapting the full machine-learning lifecycle, from defining the clinical objective through data curation/annotation, ETL standardization and anonymization, model development, and deployment via a RESTful API with continuous performance monitoring, specifically for fetal ultrasound standard-plane detection. It aims to operationalize ML models for prenatal screening workflows while embedding explainability and environmental-sustainability principles.

emb:L2038073712.exclusion_reason: structured clinical and ultrasound-derived feature model (XGBoost/CNN-LSTM) on a hypothetical dataset, not an image-based radiology AI model

emb:L2038073718.clinical_problem: detection of fetal structural and functional anomalies (cardiac and cerebral) on second-trimester ultrasound
emb:L2038073718.patient_population: second-trimester pregnancies; dataset of 1,200 labeled fetal ultrasound images
emb:L2038073718.model_description: A convolutional-neural-network-based deep learning model was developed to automatically analyze second-trimester fetal ultrasound images (1,200 labeled images) for detection of structural and functional anomalies. Its performance was compared against traditional manual interpretation and clinical expert assessment for detecting fetal cardiac and cerebral anomalies.
emb:L2038073718.dataset_size: 1,200 labeled fetal ultrasound images, second trimester
emb:L2038073718.headline_result: improved diagnostic accuracy by up to 25% compared to conventional methods; over 93% accuracy detecting fetal cardiac and cerebral anomalies

emb:L2038073719.exclusion_reason: general narrative/perspective essay covering both ultrasound-based CHD detection and non-imaging wearable sensor technologies, not a focused study or systematic review of radiology imaging AI

emb:L2038373763.model_family: multimodal pipeline: U-Net (MRI segmentation), YOLOv8 (CT lesion detection), RuBERT NLP module (report text extraction)
emb:L2038373763.body_region: abdomen/pelvis and whole body (tumor sites for neuroblastoma and sarcomas, including lung metastases)
emb:L2038373763.clinical_problem: automated staging of neuroblastoma and pediatric sarcomas by integrating tumor segmentation, metastasis detection, and radiology report information
emb:L2038373763.patient_population: 84 pediatric patients aged 6 months to 17 years with neuroblastoma (n=50) or sarcomas (n=34), single-center retrospective cohort
emb:L2038373763.model_description: A multimodal AI system for automated cancer staging combines three deep learning modules: a U-Net for tumor segmentation on MRI, a YOLOv8-based detector for metastatic lung lesions on CT, and a RuBERT natural-language-processing module that extracts staging information from Russian-language radiology reports. The combined outputs feed a classifier that assigns overall tumor stage, benchmarked against multidisciplinary tumor board decisions in 84 children (6 months to 17 years) with neuroblastoma or sarcoma.
emb:L2038373763.dataset_size: 84 patients (50 neuroblastoma, 34 sarcomas), aged 6 months to 17 years
emb:L2038373763.headline_result: segmentation Dice 0.79 (neuroblastoma), 0.81 (sarcomas); metastasis detector sensitivity 0.95, specificity 0.85 for lung nodules; overall staging accuracy 92.8% (78/84); pipeline took 8 minutes/patient vs ~45 minutes manual; surgeons agreed with AI-generated 3D tumor models in 92% of cases

emb:L2038431362.exclusion_reason: cross-sectional survey of clinician perceptions of AI competency needs; not a study of an imaging AI model
